data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A bounded DFS search utilizing symmetry reduction and prefix-level monotonicity pruning will find a verified 45-comparator 13-input sorting network orders of magnitude faster (in terms of nodes expanded) than a naive DFS, providing a discriminating simulation of why search stalls below 45.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Symmetry reduction cannot be applied to partial networks without invalidating completeness.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Prefix-level monotonicity checks require full 8192 vector evaluation, yielding no pruning advantage.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The overhead of symmetry and prefix checks causes the pruned DFS to expand more nodes than naive DFS.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Using the 0-1 principle, any partial network can be evaluated against subsets of the 8192 binary vectors to detect early failures. By applying symmetry reduction (reflection i -> n-1-i) and pruning branches that violate monotonicity on prefixes, the search space collapses significantly. A sandboxed simulation comparing naive DFS against symmetry-pruned DFS will measure the node expansion count to reach 45 comparators, demonstrating whether structural pruning alone explains the stall at 45 or if more exotic structures are needed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
